sequence_observations.observation: The sequence opens during a stoppage at the right basket. The visible scorebug reads second quarter, 8:44; the first two Hawks scores are covered by playback controls. From 0002 the score is Hawks 36, Grizzlies 29. Players wait and reposition. The cause of the stoppage and earlier team acquisition of possession are outside the packet.

A dark-uniform home player holds the ball outside the right baseline while teammates cut through the lane. By 0037-0038 an overhead inbound pass is visibly airborne toward the paint; a dark-uniform attacker jumps to meet it at 0039. Exact release and catch instants are not fully resolved.

Dark-uniform attackers reach for the inbound ball and one rises close to the basket; the ball is subsequently visible above the lane and near the rim. The precise intervening touch/transfer between dark-uniform players and the ball crossing the rim are not confidently resolved from these small stills. A white-uniform player then collects or appears to collect the ball at the right block. No whistle audio is available and no foul outcome can be determined.

The white-uniform ball holder moves outside the right baseline and passes to a white-uniform guard inside the paint. The scorebug changes from Grizzlies 29 to blank digits at 0053 and then 31 at 0054; Hawks remain 36. The visible scoring attempt, baseline restart and displayed score support a home two-point scoring sequence, but score change alone is not treated as proof of the precise unobserved rim passage, player credit or foul.

The white-uniform away guard receives the inbound, dribbles up the near/right side, crosses the center-line area and sets up outside the right arc. The video clock runs from 8:40 at 0056 to 8:34 at 0081; the score remains 36-31. This away possession is still in progress when the packet ends.

No complete possession under a gain-of-control-to-end definition can be reconstructed with all boundaries independently established: the home possession already existed before the opening dead-ball interval (14 on the shot clock), and its original start is absent; the away possession continues beyond the final frame. A local inbound-to-apparent-score-to-next-inbound segment is visible at team level, with unresolved exact touches/rim passage. These 82 screenshots are a limited approximately 20-second feasibility capture, not continuous full-game footage or a full-game review.
